📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

valentine’s Day is the official holiday for couples—so why does the fall and winter holiday season feel like a love and relationship fest?

This time of year has literally been deemed “cuffing season”: You’re encouraged to take couples pictures at a pumpkin patch, bring a date to Thanksgiving, drink hot cocoa by the fireplace at Christmas, and have someone special to kiss at midnight on New Year’s Eve.

But even though we’ve been inundated with countless signs that this is the best time to couple up, I’m going to go out on a limb here and say that I actually think there’s no better time than the holiday season to be single.

It has been revealed that “The holidays can actually be a great time for creating our own traditions and sense of self,” relationship expert Bethany Nicole tells Cosmopolitan. “Being single over the holidays gives us a much-needed time of rest, reflection, and recalibration.”.

So instead of falling victim to the pressures of coupling up during the holidays, why not just lean into being single instead? You might even find yourself enjoying the holidays more. Why? Thought you’d never ask:.

Recent findings suggest that according to Newsweek, 65 percent of Americans admitted that they’re stressed about the amount of money they’ll spend during the holidays. And for 73 percent of them, this financial stress actually makes the holidays less enjoyable. Can you guess who people are spending most of this money on? That’s right: their children and their romantic partners.

Industry observers note that sure, you might still have to get your parents, siblings, and your weird aunt a holiday gift—but isn’t it satisfying knowing that you don’t have to budget a huge chunk of change for yet another person in your life? By staying single during the holidays, you’re actually keeping your pockets happier.

The holidays are a time to spend with loved ones. But with so many events centered around the holidays, you might be spending more of that precious time with someone you’re just getting to know instead of with your friends and family. Assuming you like your friends and family, this is not the best ratio!

Recent findings suggest that when you’re single, you can spend the holiday season with whoever you want. You can go to endless friendsgivings without having to drag along a plus-one, you can eat Thanksgiving dinner comfortably with your family without having to check on someone else, and it’s actually really fun to go out on New Year’s Eve with your best friends.

Sources indicate that on the other side of the coin, family time in general is not for the weak. I get that, because mine isn’t either. If you were in a relationship, you’d probably be panicking right now about how to explain to your partner that your aunt is really funny if you ignore that she hates your mother or that your dad salutes the turkey before he cuts into it. But when you don’t have a date to Thanksgiving, you can just enjoy the weird and disturbing quirks of your family without having to explain them away to your partner.

Having no one to scare off is a relief.

When you’re coupled up, you’re expected to be “selfless” and “generous.” Ew. When you’re single, on the other hand, you can just be your normal, selfish self—and I truly think that’s beautiful.

Someone with a partner would probably be expected to give up the last piece of the pumpkin pie or be giving with an extra big piece of turkey. But because you aren’t in a relationship, you can have as much pie as you want—without pretending like you’re not picking up the speed while eating so your partner doesn’t get more bites than you.

Industry observers note that being around your own family for the holidays is torture enough—imagine if you then had to add a partner’s family to the mix? Not just that, but you’d most likely have to pretend to like them, too. And even get to know them!

Meeting an S.O.’s friends and family is a lot of pressure. Even though the holidays are a time of joy and celebration, they’re also super stressful. And you just don’t need the added stress of trying to impress your boyfriend’s dad, who doesn’t believe women should be in leadership positions.

Recent findings suggest that sure, having a partner around the holidays is nice—doing romantic things with someone you care deeply about can really add to the experience. But if you really want a partner, you have the rest of the new year to try and find someone.

For now, I say save your money, hang out with your friends, and do what the holidays were intended for: eating pie until you’re sick.

It has been revealed that this holiday season, SHEGLAM is stocked with beauty gift sets that will appeal to the distinct personalities in your circle, from the Twihards and Potterheads to the nostalgic beauty lover and more. Keep reading to find the perfect match.

Inside, they’ll find a Marauder’s Map-inspired eyeshadow palette, a mystery lip oil topped with the Sorting Hat, blush, eyeliner, setting mist, primer, and a DIY lip gloss kit they can mix up like a custom potion.

Any frequent rewatcher will appreciate the thoughtful inside jokes hidden inside this six-piece set, including the Peephole Mini Picture Frame, Central Perk Blurring Lip Tints, a lobster-shaped lip duo, a velvet sofa-embossed blush, three kajal pencils, and an eyeshadow palette behind an iconic purple door.

Highlight drops that sparkle like the skin of a forever teen, blood-red lip tints, an eyeshadow palette as dark and moody as the weather in Forks, Washington—Twihards will be dying to get their hands on this set. Recent findings suggest that expert manifestors already have their deck of tarot cards, their crystals, and their sage to burn. Gift them something even they couldn’t have predicted: this collection packed with crystal-infused lip oils, blushlighters, and eyeshadows. Each aligns with positive affirmations, such as “I trust my intuition,” “I am abundant,” and “I am pure light.” A long-lasting setting spray and a mini bottle of actual stones complete the mystical set.

For those who proudly lean into layering on blush despite the trends, look no further than this 12-piece set. Complete with 8 matte and 4 shimmer blushes, the collection spans from soft peach to brick red to fit any makeup mood your giftee is in. The viral formulas are easy to dot on with the included sponge-tip applicator.

According to recent reports, the holiday season is the most wonderful time of year for dessert devotees. Rather than gifting them their favorite candies, go the unexpected route with an advent calendar stocked with 12 full-size beauty goodies in adorable, candy-like wrappers. Inside the colorful makeup bag, giftees will be able to tear into set-exclusive products like the Divine Berry Lip Tint, Mirror Ganache gloss, and a candy-apple-red blush. Gift a throwback-beauty enthusiast a three-piece set of liquid lipsticks with vibrant color payoff and a matte finish that feels blissfully velvety and comfortable on the lips all day (unlike the formulas we swiped on back in 2016).

Inside Anmer Hall, Kate Middleton and Prince William’s Country Retreat

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (912 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday.
  • Local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times.
  • Industry observers note that anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday. Two masked men reportedly broke into Anmer Hall, their Georgian estate in Norfolk. Located on the grounds of the Sandringham Estate, the landmark house is where the Prince and Princess of Wales like to spend holidays and weekends with their three children, and it was also where Catherine recuperated from surgery and cancer treatments in 2024.

Local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times. The estate itself was unoccupied at the time of the break-in, according to police, and the suspects remain in custody.

Industry observers note that anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage. It’s a royal residence filled with equal parts gravitas and style. Take a closer look inside below.

According to recent reports, anmer Hall is in the quaint village of Anmer in Norfolk, a coastal county in northeastern England about a three-hour drive from London. The ten-bedroom Georgian pile, built in 1802, is part of Sandringham Estate, a sprawling 20,000-acre property dotted with churches, parishes, and country houses, that has been connected to the royals since 1862. The estate’s grand residence, Sandringham House, is the country bolthole of King Charles III and Queen Camilla, where royal Christmases are famously hosted. Anmer Hall is just a five-minute drive away.

While you can book tours of Sandringham House and even rent properties on the greater estate, Anmer Hall is a private family residence. The village of Anmer includes a church and quaint cottages, many of which were built in the early 20th century for Edward VII, according to an architectural guide to Norfolk by Nikolaus Pevsner and Bill Wilson. The U.K.’s Office for National Statistics states that Anmer parish had a population of about 250 in 2017.

Industry observers note that anmer Hall was the seat of the Coldham family until Prince Albert Edward (aka the future Edward VII) purchased it in 1896 to be a part of the Sandringham Estate, Pevsner and Wilson note. The two-story house’s “charming” brick facade, made from red and brown brick, features 13 bays and dormer windows in the attic. The house underwent renovations in the years following Edward VII’s purchase.

Sources indicate that over the next century, the house was leased to numerous members of the British aristocracy, including the Duke and Duchess of Kent from 1972 to 1990, and Hugh van Cutsem, one of King Charles III’s best friends. Following the expiration of van Cutsem’s lease, the property was rented to timber company owner James Everett.

In a recent development, in 2013, two years after William and Kate’s marriage, it was rumored that the royal couple would be moving in. The pair had been renting a farmhouse in Anglesey, off the northwest coast of Wales, while Prince William worked as a helicopter pilot and while they were expecting their first child, Prince George. “[Anmer Hall] would seem to be an ideal choice in that it’s close to Grandma—but not too close,” former royal correspondent Michael Cole told the BBC. Later that year, it was confirmed that William and Kate would be moving into their latest “baby bunker” with Prince George. But they wouldn’t physically move in until two years later, when Kate was expecting their second child, Princess Charlotte, to allow time for a $2 million refurbishment, which included a new roof, additional trees for privacy, and interior improvements.

In 2017, Meghan Markle and Prince Harry stayed with William and Kate at Anmer Hall, “because the sovereign still won’t permit unwed couples to sleep together under her roof Sandringham,” according to the book Notorious Royal Marriages by Leslie Carroll.

It has been revealed that today, the Prince and Princess of Wales spend most of their time at their fresh primary royal residence Forest Lodge on the grounds of Windsor Castle—but they use Anmer as a country escape. The family also spent the Covid lockdown at Anmer Hall.

As part of the property’s improvements, the Prince and Princess of Wales tapped architect Charles Morris for the renovation and designer Ben Pentreath—the designer who overhauled Kate and William’s apartment at Kensington Palace, per House & Garden—for the interiors.

According to recent reports, pentreath’s firm describes its approach as one “that draws inspiration in equal measure from the great English practitioners of the 18th and 19th centuries, and from the 1960s and ’70s…but always infused with a fresh, modern sensibility”—and the same style can be seen in snippets of Anmer Hall that eagle-eyed viewers have spotted in the Prince and Princess of Wales’s social media feeds. The home—with its high ceilings and decorative moldings—is painted in soothing, neutral colors (though the dining room is reportedly a deep green hue) and accessorized with houseplants, antiques, and gilt-framed art.

Recent findings suggest that additional amenities on the property include a pool and a tennis court; Anmer Hall also hosts its own honeybee colony. And one last bonus: The home is even stated to be haunted by its own ghost.

Geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

#123546. 10 “Timeless” Design Choices Designers Say Will Always Be in Style

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1155 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

10 “Timeless” Design Choices Designers Say Will Always Be in Style

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1155 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor.
  • Pictured above: A refreshing sunroom with built-in bookshelves by Doniphan Moore.
  • It has been revealed that while embracing home design trends can be fun for a while, it can get really old really swiftly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Pictured above: A refreshing sunroom with built-in bookshelves by Doniphan Moore.

It has been revealed that while embracing home design trends can be fun for a while, it can get really old really swiftly. Of course, if you really like something, then by all means, decorate your home with it. However, if you’re simply reaching for the things that are popular at a current moment in time before throwing them out after you realize you don’t actually like them, then it might be time to invest in some more timeless decor.

“Ultimately, timeless design is all about creating spaces that are beautiful, functional, and meaningful,” says Abby Pendergrast, an interior stylist and set designer. “That’s why people are drawn to these classics—they make a house feel like a home, and that never goes out of style.”.

In a recent development, ahead, we asked a handful of designers to share the pieces and choices they deem timeless. From gilded mirrors to striped textiles, keep reading to see the 10 things that designers promise you’ll love for years to come.

Additional copy by Meghan Shouse.

Antique chests and dressers will never go out of style because they’re well made piece that only get better with time.

Industry observers note that “They were meant to last for many years, acting as heirloom pieces for generations to come,” states Debbie Mathews LeRoy of Debbie Mathews Antiques & Designs. They’re multifunctional to use as storage or a spare surface, and they can easily move from room to room and house to house.

“An antique chest brings history and warmth to any space,” designer Emily Jiles of Maggie Griffin Design explains. “Mixing in an antique chest gives the room a collected feel and adds character that newly introduced furniture often can't replicate.”.

Golden mirrors add a touch of elegance to any room, and they’re shockingly versatile. They can bring more luxury to a traditional style home, or they can add a historic air to a more modern space. Mathews LeRoy, however, specifically adores Louis Philippe giltwood mirrors.

In a recent development, “It can live happily in a traditional interior or fit within a transitional interior thanks to its simple arched shape with minimal decoration,” she says. “They boast understated elegance and can be beautiful in an entrance hall or foyer, dining room, living room, powder room, or bedroom!”.

In a recent development, like any classic choice, bookshelves will grow with you as your sensibility evolves and changes. They can be endlessly re-styled and adjusted to hold whatever pieces you acquire along the way. Plus, they are a kind of diary of the books you are reading and the conversations you are having.

“Literature never goes out of style. A home without books isn’t a home in my opinion. And a bookshelf acts as a blank canvas to explore your innate curatorial abilities,” says Alex Bass, founder and CEO of Art Advisory & Interior Design Studio Salon 21. “It is also something that grows with you and that you can constantly reorganize. So investing in a good one with timeless appeal is key.”.

According to recent reports, high-quality natural materials such as wood or stone just get better with time. “Using natural materials in your home is always a good idea,” says Pendergrast. “They bring warmth, texture, and that feeling of authenticity we all crave.”.

It has been revealed that wood, whether it’s flooring, furniture, or even ceiling beams, adds a cozy, lived-in vibe, while stone is durable and elegant. “Wood and stone age gracefully, developing character as the years go by. They’re versatile enough to fit into any style, from modern to rustic, which means you won’t have to worry about them ever going out of fashion,” she says.

According to recent reports, while we're on the topic of natural materials, let's not forget this inimitable combination. Marble and wood both have a knack for adding character and aging beautifully, and they're not just for kitchens. Think: Wooden chairs pulled up to a marble-topped dining table or a wood coffee table or console with a marble top. The combination is “both timeless, modern, and neutral while bringing a luxurious feel to your space,” says Bass.

Recent findings suggest that leather furniture carries memories—as a piece ages, its patina changes. And a leather chair can hold its own—the material has weight and personality that make it an excellent companion to a wide range of nearby colors, fabrics, and patterns. “It fits any type of design aesthetic, whether you’re going for something more mid-century or more traditional,” Bass notes. “I love seeing the wear in a piece, the cracks and the wrinkles.”.

Sticking with paint colors inspired by nature—such as soft blues, calming greens, whites, and warm tans—helps create a peaceful and balanced space. “These colors are easy on the eyes and make your home feel more like a retreat,” Pendergrast says. “Earthy, natural shades are always in style because they have this effortless way of grounding a space. They act like neutrals, so you can easily switch up your decor over the years without having to repaint the whole place.”.

A wooden table, such as an antique farm table, is a timeless piece worth investing in. As demonstrated in this space designed by Clara Jung of Banner Day Interiors, it grounds the room, allowing other decor choices to be light and airy. Whether it’s a coffee table, side table, or made for a dining room, “You’ll always find use for it and it’s something sturdy that will never go out of style,” Bass claims.

Stripes are a classic pattern that doesn’t ever feel too trendy. “You can throw them on curtains, rugs, or even wallpaper, and they’ll add a bit of structure without overpowering the room,” Pendergrast says. “Whether you go bold or keep it subtle, stripes always find a way to fit in.” The best part about stripes is how flexible they are. “They work with just about any style, and because they’re so simple, they won’t clash with other patterns or elements in your space,” she adds.

Industry observers note that built-in details such as crown molding or wainscoting give your space instant character. Your home may already have these features, but if it doesn’t, they are often simple additions you can implement. “These features add a little polish without feeling too stuffy, and they make the room feel more custom and unique,” Pendergrast claims. “Crown molding and wainscoting have been around for ages, and they’re not going anywhere.” These architectural details are subtle ways to add depth and elegance to a room. Even better is that they can blend with any style, whether your vibe is traditional or modern.

Omega and Swatch Just Launched a Newly introduced MoonSwatch—and No Two Are the Same

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (402 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, by MoonSwatch standards, it’s been a quiet year.
  • In a recent development, an estimated 4.5 million have been sold since the collaboration began in March 2022 (and that figure only takes us to the end of 2024).
  • The latest MoonSwatch—only the third fresh model this year, compared with 11 in 2023—is the Mission to Earthphase – Silver Snowflake.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, by MoonSwatch standards, it’s been a quiet year. Swatch has been otherwise occupied with the Audemars Piguet Royal Pop, the May release for which people lined up for six days in Latest York, police deployed tear gas in France, and which, according to Swatch Group, has generated more than 25 billion views on social media.

Not that interest in the MoonSwatch has gone away.

In a recent development, an estimated 4.5 million have been sold since the collaboration began in March 2022 (and that figure only takes us to the end of 2024). In July this year, some 1.2 million people applied to buy one of the 1,969 examples of its $570 Mission to the Moon 1969, a watch that incorporated 11 grams of 18-carat gold recycled from vintage Omega components.

The latest MoonSwatch—only the third fresh model this year, compared with 11 in 2023—is the Mission to Earthphase – Silver Snowflake.

An all-black counterpart to last winter’s all-white Cold Moon edition, it takes as its starting point the idea that no two snowflakes are alike.

Swatch has developed a digital process capable of generating millions of different snowflake patterns, one of which is laser-engraved onto the moonphase indicator of each watch. So, unusually for a mass-produced quartz watch, every example is unique.

Sources indicate that it also features the complication Swatch introduced in November 2024 and which remains exclusive to the MoonSwatch: an earthphase indicator. Where a conventional moonphase demonstrates the phases of the Moon as viewed from Earth, this does the reverse. The two displays run in opposite directions over the same 29.5-day cycle.

(How useful this is to those of us who live on Earth is debatable, but it’s one of the more original ideas in watchmaking in recent years.).

There are some nice details elsewhere on the 42mm Bioceramic watch, including Snoopy and Woodstock in the snow, a pair of miniature skis at 11 o’clock, and a tiny patch of white on the Earth representing a snow-covered Switzerland, which glows green under UV light.

As with last year’s winter edition, there’s a stipulation.

The watch goes on sale at selected Swatch stores worldwide on Black Friday, November 27. After that, until March 20, 2027, the last day of winter, you’ll only be able to buy one when it’s snowing in Switzerland.

Swatch will be providing weather updates on its website.

Cosmo editor review: “This syrupy, cherry take on the classic La Vie Est Belle fragrance is so sexy and sophisticated at the same time. With my beauty editor hat on, I'd say Ambery Saffron is a bit more woodsy than Baccarat, which dries down extremely sweet on my skin. But that's likely because it doesn't have the ambroxan and sugary notes that give BR that syrupy quality. However, I really do love the addition of orange blossom in this Dossier perfume. It creates a teensy hint of citrus that works well with jasmine and saffron.”—BG.

Industry observers note that every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Pictured above: A living room area designed by Kristen Thomas of Ink & Canvas Design.

A fresh coat of paint is one of the easiest ways to give your home a little refresh before the holidays, but you don't necessarily have to take on an entire redesign project to make an impact.

Some of the most interesting places to introduce color are the details you might normally overlook. They're relatively small surfaces, but a little paint can make them feel like intentional design features, adding character and definition without the time, expense, or commitment of repainting every wall.

It has been revealed that whether you want to make a statement, add a little contrast, or create a more interesting backdrop, there are plenty of ways to make a major visual impact with a relatively small project. Ahead, designers share the unexpected spots worth painting before the holidays and how to choose colors that feel right at home.

Window casings are an easy detail to overlook, especially when they're painted the same white as the walls and trim throughout the house. But introducing a little color around the windows “can emphasize the proportions of a window and give the room more definition,” says designer Sarah Cole. Even if you're not ready to go bold, she adds that “a subtle contrast can make a difference.”.

For a more traditional look, Kristen Thomas of Ink & Canvas Design recommends pulling from a historical or traditional palette, pointing out that “colored trim was once a sign of status in early American homes” because rich pigments were costly and difficult to come by.

According to recent reports, when time is tight before the holidays, this simple painting project can be achieved in a single afternoon. Just don’t forget the painter’s tape.

Don't overlook the design impact of the interior doors in your home—a hallway lined with plain white doors can feel a little forgettable, but painting one or two in a contrasting shade can give the space a more intentional look. Paint it early enough, and you may be able to hang a wreath from it.

It has been revealed that massimo Buster Minale, founder and creative director of Buster + Punch, believes an accent like this “can completely shift the character of a room.” And you don't necessarily need to choose a bright or dramatic color to get that effect. Picking one you love, rather than going all-in on a trendy shade, is key.

“I recommend choosing a grounding color and adding some whimsy with the small touches,” notes Lee Crowder, National Director of Design and Model Experience at Taylor Morrison. Before painting, take a look at the doors in adjoining rooms so you can decide whether a single standout door or a more consistent color story makes the most sense.

If you have built-in bookshelves or cabinetry, you already have a natural spot for a little color. Rather than repainting the entire unit, try painting just the back panels. This also gives you the opportunity to declutter what’s already there. Cole recommends this pre-holiday spot because “it adds depth and helps books and collections stand out.” Her advice for choosing a shade? “Pull a color from the room's upholstery, rug or artwork.”.

According to recent reports, thomas also recommends painting built-in shelving and cabinetry as a way to create a special feature in the room. “Painting built-ins sets them apart as a special feature and creates a beautiful backdrop for your favorite objects and holiday decor,” she claims.

Instead of going for a bold contrasting hue, Vivian Robins at Arketa Design Studio suggests using a color that already appears elsewhere in the space, explaining that this small paint update can work as a “punctuation mark” in the room.

“Sometimes the smallest design changes create the biggest impression within a room because you're drawing out a color that lives in the space,” Robins adds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if Eloise had the Plaza, Valentina De Santis had the Grand Hotel Tremezzo, the luxury Lake Como resort her family has owned and operated for three generations. A Como native who spent her early career consulting at Bain & Company, she began working at the property in an official capacity in 2010, the year of its centenary. “Unofficially,” she tells us, “I clocked in as a child, running through the corridors and convinced the whole hotel depended on me.”.

Sources indicate that in 2016, De Santis took over as CEO and, by 2022, she and her parents had bought a nearby 18th-century villa and transformed it into another five-star hotel, Villa Passalacqua. As De Santis’s portfolio continues to expand, she finds comfort in working with her family and the team that’s known her for her whole life: “People who grow with you, believe in what you are building, and care about it as much as you do, that’s everything.”.

In our On the Couch survey, we asked De Santis about all the places, people, and pieces that inspire her. She also divulges a few of her best travel recommendations—both in Como and beyond.

Describe your studio in three words: Full. Of. Chaos.

Greatest Influences: My parents, my first and forever creative directors.

Favorite Eras of Design: The Belle Époque, when more was more and every room seemed to have a little champagne in its veins.

It has been revealed that favorite Sofa: A Daisy curved Italian midcentury sofa from the 1950s. It's beautifully sculptural, it's pink. It's Gio Ponti.

In a recent development, maverick design style trick: Break one rule. If everything in a room is behaving, something is missing.

Most beloved buildings: Villa Necchi Campiglio in Milan. When I lived in the city, it was right on my doorstep, so I was there all the time. And always, always a little hello to the pink flamingos next door!

Architect you admire: Not the big name you’d expect, but the one closest to my heart, Ico Parisi. He made a real difference in my family’s story. He taught my parents how to look at art, and how to love it, and I grew up seeing the world through that same eye.

In a recent development, destination Museum: The Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice and the Fondation Maeght in Saint-Paul-de-Vence. Before they were museums, they were the homes of great collectors, and it reveals. You half expect the host to walk in and offer you a drink. With Casabianca, we hope to bring the same magic to my parents’ collection. Peggy, I hope you approve.

Go-to galleries: Lia Rumma in Milan. It has a strong point of view and never plays it safe. It is where we found one of Anselm Kiefer’s Women of Antiquity, which now lives at Casabianca. I’ll never forget my mother’s face the day we saw her; that was when we knew she was coming home with us.

Favorite Artist: Mark Rothko. My wildest dream is to have one in my living room, one of those enormous canvases where color doesn’t just sit on the surface; it explodes, then slowly pulls you in.

Sources indicate that vintage Piece of Your Dreams: An original Margherita by Franco Albini for Bonacina. Yes, I know, more from the ’50s! I clearly have a type. I love how sculptural it is, while the woven rattan keeps it feeling warm and relaxed.

It has been revealed that favorite getaway: Puglia. I have spent so many summers there with my family that it feels like a second home.

Hotels to Check Into: The Amalfi Coast is hard to beat. In my opinion, some of the best hotels in the world are concentrated in just a few miles, each one an incredible house. On top of that, they are all dear friends, so I would love to check into every one of them. But my favorite memory? Lemon linguine on the terrace of the Santa Caterina.

According to recent reports, best Shop for Gifts: Chez Dédé in Rome. Daria and Andrea are dear friends, and the co-authors of our Passalacqua book, and everything in their shop seems to come with a story. My favorite is their Lettera d’Amore necklace, a love letter you can actually wear.

Sources indicate that best Host/Hostess Gift: Something made with your own hands, or close enough! Olive oil from your grove, homemade biscuits, chocolate-dipped orange peel. Add a handwritten note, and it beats anything you could ever buy.

Entertaining Tips: Always have more food than you need. Italian mothers have taught me this much.

Sources indicate that style Icons: Lady Di. I’ve had a crush on her since I was a little girl, and honestly, I never got over it.

It has been revealed that fashion Designers: JJ Martin (La DoubleJ) for the extraordinary way JJ brings color, print, and joy into fashion. Emilia Wickstead for her beautiful, feminine silhouettes.

Style Tip: Go tone-on-tone. My friend Patrizia, who designs Moresi's collections, taught me there's nothing chicer than a head-to-toe single-color look.

Sources indicate that required Reading: Va' dove ti porta il cuore by Susanna Tamaro. It is the book I have turned to whenever I have had a major decision to make, and somehow it always brings me back to the same place: follow your heart.

According to recent reports, cocktail of Choice: A Bellini. It is hard to improve on a classic.

According to recent reports, favorite Restaurant: La Tirlindana on the lake for old-world magic. In Milan, I stay loyal to the classics: Da Giacomo and Savini never miss.

Must-Have Accessory: A great pair of unscratchable sunglasses. I live by a lake, so they are both a fashion accessory and a survival tool.

In a recent development, watch to Wear: A Cartier Tank Louis Cartier in yellow gold. It has been chic for so long that it has nothing left to prove.

According to recent reports, favorite Jeweler: Felice Gabaglio in Como. I have known Marina and her family for as long as I can remember. My father used to take me there to choose jewelry for my mother, and I was always so excited to discover those little treasures with him. It is still where I go when I want something truly special. And now Marina’s daughters have released JAM, a new contemporary line of their own. So now I have another very good reason to stop by.

Annie Goldsmith is the senior editor and digital lead at ELLE Decor, where she covers design, culture, style, and trends. She previously held positions at The Information, covering technology and culture, and Town & Country, writing about news, entertainment, and fashion. Her work has also appeared in Vogue, Rolling Stone, and the SF Standard.

The 6 Best Gaming Headsets for All Types of Players

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that nothing truly makes me feel immersed in a game the same way good sound does.
  • If you consider gaming your main hobby, you’re probably either a single-player person or you like to squad up in your battle royale of choice.
  • Sources indicate that here's the problem.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that nothing truly makes me feel immersed in a game the same way good sound does. And it’s impossible to get that level of tension in a horror game like Resident Evil, or the feeling of being absolutely locked in a competitive shooter without a good pair of headphones. Nowadays, video games are fully open world of 3D and spatial audio, and there's never been a better time to hop on the bandwagon. It's time to get a gaming headset.

If you consider gaming your main hobby, you’re probably either a single-player person or you like to squad up in your battle royale of choice. It doesn’t matter, actually, because the only proper way to experience both ends of the gaming spectrum is with a headset. For single-player, that means fully immersive audio. For multiplayer, you’ll sound crystal clear to your teammates—no more confusion or excuses. The good noise-canceling headsets even have transparency modes so you don’t have to ignore everyone in your real life either.

Sources indicate that here's the problem. There are actually plenty of good headsets and trustworthy brands that make dozens of similar options. Finding the headset that will work for you isn’t made to be easy, but that’s why I’m here. I know my gaming headsets like the back of my hand—that’s my job. To figure out if you need a high-end wireless SteelSeries headset, or if you’ll be happy with a sub-$100 option, read on. Hell, maybe you’d prefer earbuds. I’ve accounted for all options.

This is the one gaming headset I won’t (and frankly can’t) say anything negative about. I suppose that’s what $600 gets you. SteelSeries has long made comfortable headsets that support multiple platforms with easy swapping. It introduced the world to its GameHub base station, letting you connect all your systems to one panel and easily control them all from there.

Sources indicate that the Nova Elite takes every already perfectly solved puzzle piece and puts a little extra sheen on it. First off, it is gorgeous, with exteriors made from premium steel, aluminum, and vegan leather. Nothing else in the gaming space compares to it in terms of the luxe look. In terms of fit, the Nova Elite distributes its weight evenly so you can play for hours without discomfort.

In a recent development, and this headset’s gaming hub has an extra feature that really changes things. The hot-swappable batteries are SteelSeries’ biggest innovation in recent years, and here the hub also acts as a charger for your second (included) headset battery. So whichever one is not powering your current session is being charged. What this means is battery life is a solved problem. You literally never have to worry about running out of charge mid-game again. And for some, that alone might be worth the price of admission.

Recent findings suggest that okay, forget what I just said. This is everything a wireless headset needs to be for the average gamer. ASUS has targeted a lower price point and succeeded in terms of knowing which features to cut, and what to keep to make it still feel like a high-quality experience. You don't get active noise cancellation or the ability to play audio from two sources at once. For those luxuries, go for the Delta II.

It has been revealed that at 0.7 pounds, the Pelta is remarkably light and the furthest thing from bulky. It's about letting you play all day on those summer Saturdays where it's too hot to go outside. Where it surprises in this regard is battery life. Offering up to 70 hours between charges and a fit that won't leave you itchy and sweaty, this is the all-nighter-friendly headset.

While I wouldn't personally spring for a wired headset, those who do are hard to convince otherwise. And that crowd has spent the last couple of years rallying around the HyperX Cloud Alpha. If competitive gaming is the reason you are turning to a headset, this has everything you need for under $100.

You aren't going to get the audio options you do from the multi-hundred-dollar headsets SteelSeries and Corsair sell. Instead, you are paying a reasonable price for a high-quality microphone, and a comfortable pair of headphones. Stop worrying about lag and stop worrying about your headset running out of battery. It's time to wire in.

According to recent reports, when it comes to sound quality, the Corsair Virtuoso Max brings it to a new level. This is a better-sounding headset than most of the readers of this article have ever experienced.

In a recent development, my favorite high-tech touch that we actually use is the simultaneous connection. Using the 2.4 GHz dongle and Bluetooth in tandem you can get the audio from your game and audio from a Bluetooth source at the same time. That means pumping in your own tunes or a background podcast while grinding levels. When playing with friends, I love the addition of a physical, sturdy, functional mic mute button.

The only glitch is long-term comfort. Weighing in at just under a pound, the 60-hour battery life on the headset is a bit of a moot point. You'll want to take it off anyway because it can start to feel quite hard on your skull after a couple hours of white knuckle gaming.

It has been revealed that if you have a single gaming machine and that console is a PS5, this is the headset I recommend. It is remarkably lightweight, weighing even less than the wired-only pair I recommended earlier, and it’s super easy to use—with a satisfying mute button that pops in and out, and a microphone that is entirely detachable. So if you’re settling in for a night of solo horror gaming, you can set the mic aside and still enjoy the excellent sound and spatial audio options. And if you know that battery is low, or you really just want the easiest solution, the package includes a 3.5mm cable for wired connection. Just plug that right into your DualSense controller and you’re off to the races.

It has been revealed that beyond just PlayStation diehards, this is an excellent option for any PC or Nintendo gamer who wants a light wireless headset. It is fully compatible via USB-C transceiver or headphone cable with any other modern console, sans the Xbox.

Okay, so I lied. When you clicked on this for the six best headsets, yeah one of these isn't a gaming headset at all. It's a set of earbuds designed by SteelSeries to be used on gaming consoles and it's as much of a game-changer as it sounds. If you feel cheated, don't fret. There are two more headsets listed in the honorable mentions below. Please accept my humble offering.

Recent findings suggest that if you’ll allow me to talk about them for just a minute though, the Arctis GameBuds are just shy of a miracle. They are comfy earbuds with all-encompassing noise-canceling (gasp!), spatial audio support, and a very useful transparency/talk-through mode. The sound isn't quite on par with SteelSeries's larger headsets, but it still impresses. Plus, unlike the rest of these headsets, you can fit them in your pocket.

In a recent development, steelSeries Arctis Nova 7 ($179): You don't need to shell out for the Nova Elite to get a good Arctis headset. This one uses a simple USB-C dongle, so isn't nearly as complicated to set up, either.

Turtle Beach Stealth Pro 2: ($349): My favorite fresh headset of the year. An excellent multi-platform choice with high-quality playback and call audio. It also uses a swappable battery system, so you never run out of charge in a heated gaming moment.

What We Look for in a Gaming Headset.

It has been revealed that testing gaming headsets really isn't too difficult. You make sure it's compatible with what it states on the box, and then tell the people if it’s comfortable and if it sounds good. Shit simple until you do it enough to realize a simple truth. Most models from reputable brands are worth their costs, and very few companies have duds in their lineups. That remarked, there are ways to tell what's going to rise from the crop. Here's some pointers for the next time you shop for headsets.

In a recent development, comfort — If you can't stay comfortable in them for more than an hour they are going straight in the trash. Even the most uncomfortable among these picks are still in the top 5% of comfortable gaming headphones.

Sound Quality — Like with the pair of headphones you use to listen to music, you want clear sound with plenty of range.

In a recent development, microphone — If you're gaming online, your microphone needs to cut out unwanted background noise. Some offer noise cancelling, some just have good unidirectional builds. All on this list are great in this department.

Directional Sound — Spatial audio is cool when watching movies, but when playing games this can take your team play to the next level. When you hear an enemy's footsteps, you can know they're behind you at four o'clock, not six. And that makes you an asset. It also makes the taste of victory that much sweeter.

Connection — I will discuss wireless vs. wired shortly, but when it comes to the going wireless there's usually two ways to connect a gaming headset. Bluetooth or via a USB dongle. The latter typically has less latency and is the preferred way to connect.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

Are wired or wireless headsets better for gaming?

It has been revealed that if you care about latency (aka lag), we are going to recommend wired over wireless. The added hassle of wireless charging and connecting doesn't necessarily make up for the hassle of having a wire. Plus, you don't have to worry about it not working on some devices—which you do with pretty much every wireless device you buy.

Do all gaming headsets work across all platforms?

Sources indicate that I'm glad you asked. No! As you may have noticed, there tend to be two kinds of headsets. Those that work with Xbox.. and those that work with everything else. Since Xbox uses its own wireless standard instead of Bluetooth. In practice, this means Xbox gamers need to be extra careful when buying headsets to make sure the one they're getting is compatible. SteelSeries, for example, sells two versions of each headset, one marked for Xbox.

It has been revealed that it's actually more complicated than "all headsets that work with PC also work with PlayStation and you have to get ones especially for Xbox," but in many of these cases that is the gist. Although the PlayStation headsets work on PC and Mac but not Nintendo Switch. So, yeah, it's pretty inconsistent. Seriously, just read the list of compatible platforms before you buy a headset.

For the event, Kate wore an oxblood, floor-length Anarkali dress by designer Mahima Mahajan and paired it with extra-fluffy, voluminous bohemian curls pinned in a half-updo.

An elegant, extra-glossy wavy hairstyle has long been a beauty signature for the princess, often teamed with a side part, hats, or a polished ponytail. But for the green carpet in India, the royal opted for a much more dramatic style that matches the glamorous mood of her outfit, with tighter, cascading bohemian curls woven into a beautiful half-updo twist for a romantic finish.

Recent findings suggest that "I would create these curls using a medium-sized tong," recommends Philipp Haug, co-founder of Haug London Haus salon. "Take relatively small sections and use the tongs with a twisting technique, curling one section away from the face and alternating with one section towards the face throughout. To enhance the fluffiness and volume of the curls, shake them out with your fingers instead of combing them.

Your next special occasion hair inspiration, sorted.

7 Home Organizing Trends That Will Be EVERYWHERE in 2027, According to Pros

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that although trends prevail in the interior design world, they also can find their way into other areas beyond decor—such as home organization.
  • As we look to the year ahead, four professional organizers are here to share what they think will be the top organizing trends.
  • While AI has been all over the place, from work to our personal lives—it appears to be tapering off, according to Lenora O’Keith, decluttering and organizing expert and owner of Aronel Home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that although trends prevail in the interior design world, they also can find their way into other areas beyond decor—such as home organization. Creating orderly spaces can make life a lot easier. While tried-and-true solutions are still around, there are always fresh ways to tackle organizing projects.

As we look to the year ahead, four professional organizers are here to share what they think will be the top organizing trends.

While AI has been all over the place, from work to our personal lives—it appears to be tapering off, according to Lenora O’Keith, decluttering and organizing expert and owner of Aronel Home.

It has been revealed that “AI and smart home solutions were everywhere at the beginning of the year, but there’s definitely been a lot of AI fatigue and a push for ‘dumb tech’ lately,” she shares. “When working with clients, a lot of them are over AI being added into everything. They just want simple solutions that work.” This can include things like setting up a household command center and labeling storage containers.

Moving has traditionally been a stressful experience that you were expected to figure out on your own—but that may be changing. Allison Flinn, owner of Reclaim Professional Organizing, notes that more people are taking advantage of organizing services when they move.

“You can pack and unpack, but you won't truly have a fully functional and an organized new home if you haven't decluttered prior to moving or aren't intentional during the unpacking process by implementing a system that truly works for your lifestyle,” she indicates.

Instead of doing what a lot of us do—devising storage systems for each individual space—2027 may welcome the idea that you should treat your home as an entire unit to be organized.

According to recent reports, michelle Urban, owner and founder of The Organized House, states that people are increasingly not treating each room as its own one-off organizing project. She says that instead, they’re looking at how belongings move from one space to another and where they need to be throughout the day. For instance, items like backpacks, shoes, and sports gear may land in the entry, get stored in the garage, and need to be back by the door the next morning.

“When those spaces are planned together, the system supports the family’s routine instead of just moving things from one pile to another,” Urban states.

Viewed more holistically, experts are also seeing that organizing isn’t just an occasional task, but something to stay on top of each week. “I think more homeowners will begin to view organization as ongoing home maintenance rather than a one-time project,” says Ashley Bailey, founder and professional organizer at Everything Orderly. “Just like other aspects of maintaining a home, organizing requires occasional attention as our lives and needs change.”.

Flinn indicates that more and more people are outsourcing household tasks to a home manager or home concierge. In addition to handling things like doing laundry, returning packages, and making doctor’s appointments, these professionals can also help you organize your home in just a few hours a week.

Sources indicate that eco-friendly everything is still as popular as ever, and it even applies to how we organize our homes. While O’Keith indicates that sustainability never really goes out of style, homeowners are increasingly turning to eco-friendly organizing products—specifically, by avoiding plastic and embracing natural materials like bamboo, rattan, and sea grass for baskets and bins.

But she indicates that there is a exception for basements and attics. “I always recommend heavy-duty plastic storage [for these areas],” O’Keith says. “Since those spaces deal with dampness, temperature changes, and pests, other materials could get damaged easily.”.

Recent findings suggest that while it can be lovely to live in a well-designed, beautiful home, if there isn’t function, you might make your daily life more difficult. That’s why people are going beyond Instagram-ready interiors and are wrapping in plenty of function.

Urban believes that progressively more people are bringing functional storage into a room’s design, and it isn’t just an add-on.

“A credenza can hold games in the living room; a dining room buffet can store wrapping paper and party decor between celebrations,” Urban points out. “As rooms take on more jobs, people want storage that looks like it belongs and does a useful job.”.

As we head into 2027, people are thinking about their budgets more and more, which is why using items you already have as storage solutions is cost-effective.

In a recent development, “I'm seeing more clients interested in making better use of what they already own rather than automatically purchasing new organizing products,” Bailey says. For instance, she recently took on a project that transformed a playroom, but used items the family already had.

“Sometimes the best solution isn't another organizing product. It's rethinking how you're using the space and what you already have,” she indicates. “I think we'll see more emphasis on thoughtful editing and repurposing before purchasing something upcoming.”.

Latest Update: “Two Girls Who Speak All the Time About Politics”: Tao Okamoto and Virginie Efira Take On Capitalism in All of a Sudden

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1827 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that we’re all seeking comfort as the world ends.
  • According to recent reports, all of a Sudden tells the story of two women who forge a formidable friendship as they face personal and professional hardship.
  • Sources indicate that the film is an adaptation of a nonfiction book, When Life Suddenly Takes a Turn: Twenty Letters Between a Philosopher With Terminal Cancer and a Medical Anthropologist, which collects correspondence from two Japanese-speaking academics as they reflect on health care and death during the last few months of philosopher Makiko Miyano’s life (who inspired Okamoto’s character).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we’re all seeking comfort as the world ends. Environmental, economic, and political pressures weigh heavily on our minds as tangible solutions feel farther and farther out of reach. Solace is a rare commodity in a world controlled by unrelenting capitalist forces. In All of a Sudden, filmmaker Ryusuke Hamaguchi suggests that as we face tragedy, we must remember our vital need for human connection.

According to recent reports, all of a Sudden tells the story of two women who forge a formidable friendship as they face personal and professional hardship. Marie-Lou Fontaine (Virginie Efira) runs an elder-care facility near Paris, where she introduces a “Humanitude” methodology designed to treat patients with dignity and introduce listening-heavy caretaking practice. She befriends Mari (Tao Okamoto), a terminally ill theater director from Japan. Ryusuke chronicles this relationship through extended, emotional conversations, spoken in both Japanese and French, and covering topics from identity to mortality.

Sources indicate that the film is an adaptation of a nonfiction book, When Life Suddenly Takes a Turn: Twenty Letters Between a Philosopher With Terminal Cancer and a Medical Anthropologist, which collects correspondence from two Japanese-speaking academics as they reflect on health care and death during the last few months of philosopher Makiko Miyano’s life (who inspired Okamoto’s character). Instead of keeping the fact that the two pen pals spoke the same language, he introduced French and moved the story to Paris. This small change forced the story to confront language gaps, exploring the power of conversation and listening and asserting that so much can be achieved through this mediation.

In a recent development, efira and Okamoto understand their characters’ simmering anxieties and outlooks on the world, providing the bedrock for these impressively naturalistic performances. The two actresses sustain long, philosophical conversation with such intensity throughout the entire three hours and 16 minutes. In a rare occurrence, the two shared the Best Actress Award at the Cannes Film Festival, where the movie premiered this summer. In the film, their budding friendship serves as a sounding board for each other, as Marie-Lou grapples with the pressure of capitalism on her medical staff and Mari comes to terms with the end of her life. In typical fashion, Ryusuke lets the camera linger on these two actresses during these prolonged philosophical interactions, forcing the audience to sit with the gravity of their situations.

Ahead of the theatrical release of Ryusuke’s latest feature film, Bazaar spoke to Efira and Okamoto about the first time they read the script, how they built an intimate bond despite speaking two different languages, and the punk, anti-capitalist edge fueling this intimate, conversation-heavy film.

Tao Okamoto: It’s the scene where she talks about capitalism while writing on the whiteboard. That’s one of the strangest scenes in the movie. I felt connected to the character because I am also a climate activist myself. I’ve been spreading the word about climate crises on podcasts, and I talk about it daily. When I read the part, I felt, “I need to play this character.”.

Virginie Efira: It’s the same for me, because this scene is so special. When I read it, the movie felt like one of the most profound, special, and radical readings. You have two girls who speak all the time about politics. We don’t see that. I never see that in other movies. Sometimes, when a director wants to put something philosophical, political, or intellectual, they say, “Maybe we’ll do three minutes,” otherwise the audience will be bored. No, this movie spent 15 minutes [discussing capitalism], and I noted, “Oh yes, that’s so punk!” The film has its own language. When I read All of a Sudden, I could hear the language of the movie, and I wanted to approach it. When I met Tao, I thought, “Oh, we are so lucky to be an actress and work with [Ryusuke], but also to share this material with him.”.

Recent findings suggest that VE: I only knew one word in Japanese before making the movie. Then, to be able to speak Japanese at a high level, because the character studied in Japan, I must first learn to read, then learn to embody the language. Finding the language of the movie was strange. There’s a flat and natural way to play [in one of Ryusuke’s movies]. He spoke to me about Cassavetes and Gena Rowlands, but also about Bresson. Neutral performances. You find it when you open up, and when I opened to Tao, we discovered the right language for the movie. We did a lot of flat readings before shooting. We never rehearsed in motion, so when we finally performed for the first time, we awakened the text.

In a recent development, TO: I’m going to add that because I started my career in America, finding a middle ground by using a language that’s not my mother tongue is normal for me. On the surface, that part wasn’t a challenge for me. Finding the language for this film and respecting Hamaguchi’s way of working were priorities. We were naturally drawn to his talent and wanted to make his dream happen and be part of it.

Sources indicate that TO: I joined this project way after Virginie. I luckily had months to prepare with him, and during rehearsals, you drop all emotion and read the text as if you were reading numbers. On top of that, I got to visit some institutes, such as the Cancer Research Center and places where people work with disabled people, to build up my understanding of my role’s point of view. Reading the text over and over was a unique experience for me. [Ryusuke] can really listen to the actor’s voice and tell the difference between someone who is simply reading and someone really concentrating. Even though you’re not supposed to put any emotions, you have to be present; you have to be there. I’ve never experienced such rich, profound preparation for a role.

VE: We shot in a real nursing home. There was a mix between fiction and reality. Sometimes filmmaking becomes standardized, with no room left to breathe, but with Hamaguchi, you’re sure he will leave room for the unexpected and for uncertainty. It allows you to embrace the unpredictability of reality. He’s not looking for an accident, but for the ability to be in the present. A viewer of Hamaguchi’s work will always feel a sensation of documentation, but it’s still always cinema. To be an actor in his movies is to be naturalistic, to be in the present, to capture some details and really embrace this unpredictability. The filming process becomes an adventure he wants you to have. One day, he told me, “I hope that you will find the light.” He remarked a lot of cryptic things. He said to me, “Don’t use your text like a tool; just go inside the text.”.

TO: The script is already amazing. And I could read it over and over again, and that was a joy. But he mentioned that I should read the original book. It’s about two women exchanging letters—or emails. They are real people who the characters are modeled after. I wanted to please the people who know these women, not to make them too different from them. I first put pressure on myself to portray this woman as close to the real person, but it was impossible for me because this person passed away in 2019. I couldn’t do much research, so I interviewed her mother and the co-writer. That provided me with a lot of clues, but reading their exchanged letters already gave me the soul of this movie.

VE: He gives the book to the actresses, but also to the entire team. I never felt something so collective, and you will feel it in the movie, from the sound engineer to someone who only stayed two days on set. I also met the anthropologist. When you read this book, it’s full of life. It gives you a perceptible beauty of things. The book has a kind of energy; it helps you keep a level of optimism even when you know the situation is hopeless. In this book, it speaks about what it’s like to be alive. Maybe there’s beauty in life because we are going to die.

According to recent reports, TO: For me, I came on this project at the last minute, only a month before. Virginie was so dedicated to studying Japanese from scratch; it was so impressive how she studied all this writing, reading, and lines. Seeing that, I had a huge admiration, like “Who can do this!?” As you can see, Virginie’s so charming; nobody would hate her. It was so easy for me to be drawn to her as a person, as the characters in the movie were discovering each other.

VE: We got to know each other through the shoot. I was happy not to know much at the beginning and to progressively get deeper into our relationship. We lived all that together. I conflate Marie-Lou’s feelings for Mari with Virginie’s feelings for Tao, because we share that. It will be an end, not a tragic one like in the movie, but it will be an end. But I know Tao will carry this experience in her heart forever, and I will too. He let us feel what we want to feel.

According to recent reports, TO: I study environmental issues, and I always thought capitalism is responsible for our world’s issues. Something I didn’t know until I read this script was that capitalism doesn’t only exploit our environment, but also our human bodies—human labor and our time. When I connected those dots, I realized all the problems could be blamed on capitalism. We’re looking for time and looking for happiness—or security—and all these things can be related to a capitalistic way of living. I think it’s great that Hamaguchi connected that fundamental matter to Marie-Lou’s situation in the elderly home. She’s frustrated, as is Marie. She’s battling her cancer, and it can be connected to this economic issue.

In a recent development, VE: Cinema can show bodies, fatigue, and with Marie-Lou, you see a certain fatigue because capitalism creates it. How do we deal with that? We say, “Oh, capitalism’s not good. We don’t have time. And we want to be richer and richer.” But how do we fight that, because everything is already there? I come from France, and you see all the young people outside. The real question is, what can cinema do with that? It’s not a theoretical thing, but Hamaguchi can find a solution. It’s speaking, listening to the other, sharing ideas; it’s movement. If I look for a solution to this problem with money, I’ll remain a prisoner of this way of functioning. Even if you think you’re not in a stage of capitalism, you are.

This interview has been condensed and edited for clarity.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • These luxurious leather gloves come from Overland, the brand behind some of our favorite coats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there are few winter experiences more miserable than stepping outside with bare hands and realizing, too late, that your fingers have stopped working. First they’re freezing, then they’re numb, and before long your skin feels dry and rough and beyond the help of any hand lotion.

But honestly? Gloves can be annoying, too. Some turn a quick phone check into a whole production; others are so bulky you might as well be wearing oven mitts. The best winter gloves keep your hands warm without making your fingers useless—and look good while they’re at it. We’ve rounded up our favorites, from waterproof, windproof pairs built for rough weather to stylish options that still keep your hands nice and toasty. And yes, plenty have touchscreen-compatible fingertips so you can still call and text (and play the Wordle). See our favorite pairs below.

These luxurious leather gloves come from Overland, the brand behind some of our favorite coats. The smooth leather looks very polished, so these gloves can be dressed up if you want, but they go just as well with a casual outfit. They’re also quite durable and are naturally water-repellant, and the cashmere lining adds warmth on the inside.

Industry observers note that commerce Editor Luke Guillory loves these merino wool-lined deerskin gloves from Geier Gloves, a brand that has been making leather products in the U.S. for almost a century. Since the brand specializes in leather, you can bet the deerskin on these gloves is of the highest quality, and the wool lining is very nice, too. Geier also makes a lot of wor, driving, and motorcycle gloves, so you know they’re the real deal. The black and brown colorways look quite polished, but the natural and saddle leather options are also great.

Recent findings suggest that if you want a nice luxurious pair of cashmere gloves, go with these ones from Sunspel. Lately, I’ve been wearing these gloves, which were knitted in Scotland from super soft pure cashmere. The brand has been perfecting the craft for over 150 years, so you can trust that these are the best of the best. It’s basically like enveloping your hands in a cozy blanket. For a full set, get the brand’s cashmere hat and scarf.

Sources indicate that these Canada Goose gloves are basically the equivalent of wearing a puffer jacket on your hands. With heavy-duty, long rib-knit cuffs for extra protection and 750-fill-power down on the inside, your hands will stay warm and dry without their mobility being super impacted by something extra bulky. Note that these have a touchscreen-compatible index finger but not thumb.

In a recent development, wool-blend gloves are as handsome as any of the very best sweaters in your rotation. Even though the outside is made from knit material, the insulated interior will keep your hands warm and dry during your next epic snowball fight. They’re also thin enough to layer under another pair of gloves if it’s really freezing outside.

According to recent reports, when it comes to gloves, there’s one brand I’ve trusted for years, and that’s Smartwool. Their gloves are warm without being bulky, and mine have lasted for years. Having a warm pair of gloves that actually does its job well is even more important for my boyfriend, who has Raynaud’s and needs extra protection for his hands, and the gloves he relies on year after year? Also Smartwool. These newly introduced fleece gloves from the brand have extra insulation on the back to provide serious warmth, and they’re also functional with touchscreen-compatible pads on the thumbs and index fingers. Sure, they’re a little expensive for fleece gloves at $68—but if you don’t need the extra insulation, you can try the regular Active Fleece Gloves for $48.

Recent findings suggest that if all you need is a solid pair of knit gloves and you’re not looking to spend a fortune, look no further than Uniqlo. The brand’s Heattech knit gloves are soft and warm and have effective touchscreen-compatible fingertips. They also come in 11 fun colors, so you might as well get a couple pairs for yourself—and they make a great holiday gift for literally anyone.

You already know we love Barbour’s waxed canvas jackets, so it’s no surprise we’re also a fan of the brand’s stylish, preppy gloves. These leather-palmed gloves have a cotton tartan face for a cool contrast and wool lining on the inside for extra warmth—and they’re waterproof, so you can break them out no matter what’s going on with the weather. Pair these with the Barbour Beaufort jacket for an iconic look.

Knit gloves are great when it comes to keeping warm, but they’re not the best when it’s raining or snowing. No one wants a pair of soaking gloves (that probably make your hands feel even colder). Enter these waterproof gloves from the brand that brought you the famous Bean Boots. With a waterproof nylon exterior and a down fill, they’ll keep rain and show out while keeping your hands warm. Note that some say the fingers are long, so consider that when choosing a size.

Sources indicate that when you’re stuck in a blizzard or your location is prone to unpredictable weather, you’ll need something a little more heavy duty. REI’s weatherproof gore-tex gloves will give your hands the protection they need. They’re also essentially a two-in-one: The removable fleece liners can be used on their own or with the weatherproof outers as an extra layer of warmth.

Naadam’s famous cashmere sweater is one of our favorite pieces of winter clothing and one of our go-to gifts for the holidays, birthdays, Valentine’s Day, etc. The brand makes a matching pair of soft cashmere gloves, which come in 13 colors and are under $100. A genius gift idea? Get them the sweater with a matching pair of gloves, and they’ll wear both all winter long.

Industry observers note that if you want that classic Sherlock Holmes leather glove look, you have lots of choices. But if you don’t want to spend a ton on a pair, get these $60 gloves from Quince. Not only do they have a nice leather exterior in either brown or black, they also have a cashmere lining on the inside.

On the high end of the high end, Gucci has a gorgeous luxury pair of leather gloves with the brand’s signature horsebit on the wrist for a fun little detail. Made from leather and silk, these are soft, smooth, and very stylish.

According to recent reports, black Friday isn't until November 27, but that hasn't stopped mattress brands from getting a head start on the holiday savings. If your current bed has seen better days or you're waking up with more aches than you went to bed with, there's no need to wait until a designated shopping day to save substantial on an upgrade. We've spotted the 12 best Black Friday mattress deals to explore ahead of all of your Thanksgiving festivities.

Sources indicate that brands like Saatva, Birch, and Beautyrest are already offering up to $1,000 off on hotel-worthy innerspring mattresses, cooling hybrids, and organic options. Whether you're a side sleeper in need of a little extra cushioning for your hips and shoulders or someone who prefers a firmer, more supportive surface, there's something worth considering before the holiday rush kicks into high gear.

Industry observers note that below, you'll find AD-tested mattresses, complete with reviewer insights, notable features, and details about the current promotions. Get ready to find your next bed without losing sleep over the price tag.

It has been revealed that saatva is giving shoppers who have “luxury mattress” on their Black Friday wish list a head start on savings. The brand is taking over $600 off its popular Classic queen. Designed to deliver hotel-worthy comfort at home, the innerspring mattress features a dual-coil construction; a plush, three-inch Euro pillow top; and targeted lumbar support that helps promote spinal alignment. It also comes in three firmness options—plush soft, luxury firm, and firm—making it a versatile choice for different sleep positions. Reviewer Erin Kaplan, a combination side-and-stomach sleeper, praises the mattress's supportive feel, durability, and temperature regulation. “Overall, I get a better night’s sleep on a more consistent basis since I switched mattresses,” she indicates. Complimentary white-glove delivery, a 365-night sleep trial, and a lifetime warranty round out the perks of this high-end buy.

It has been revealed that another name brand with an impressive 180 years of history, Stearns & Foster has a reputation for hotel-quality bedding you’ll find in luxury hotel chains like the Ritz-Carlton. They’ve already kicked off their Black Friday sale, which promises up to $1,000 off select adjustable mattress sets and a $300 Visa gift card with all mattress purchases. Senior visuals editor Melissa Maria raves about her Stearns & Foster Lux Estate Mattress, noting its seamless white glove delivery service was a game-changer. The level of firmness required an adjustment period for her, but the Tempur-Indulge memory foam layer and added pillow top gave it a more plush feel. “I’m a very light and finicky sleeper and it always takes me time to adjust to any sort of change, but my husband remarked at how well he slept and how much better his back felt after the first couple of nights sleeping on this mattress,” she claims.

It has been revealed that beautyrest’s long-lasting mattresses are powered with advanced pocketed coil technology, helping couples with motion isolation and providing zoned support. The brand’s Black Friday sale is underway, and you can now save up to $1,000 on select mattress and adjustable base sets. Audience development manager Emma Tubbs recommends the Beautyrest Black Series One Mattress, which she indicates has the “perfect firmness.” “As someone who continuously changes positions throughout the night, the quilted innerspring construction nicely accommodated my tossing and turning,” she writes in her review. “I often fall asleep on my stomach and move to my side and even my back as I fall deeper into REM—I feel supported by this mattress in each position.” Plus, the motion isolation has worked well for her, as she continues sleeping through her husband’s 5:30 a.m. wakeups.

Over the past century, Serta’s become known for making comfortable, solidly priced mattresses. As it stands, the brand is offering the lowest price we’ve seen in months on the Serta Five-Star Mattress. Shopping writer Julia Harrison had this mattress-in-a-box delivered downstairs, and managed to haul it up with the help of her roommate. She refers to it as relatively lightweight (thanks to the gel-infused foam versus a heavier gel bead layer), exactly medium-firm, and made without any frills. “Nothing about it feels too hard or too soft, which I know primarily because I never think about the density or firmness of this mattress (a good sign!) and because I’ve had no back or neck problems since sleeping on it,” she notes.
